lean.fidelity_note: For positive scales $\ell_*,h$, a positive time weight $\gamma$, and smooth fields with the required bounded spatial and phase derivatives, the formal statement proves all of (D.3)–(D.5) and finiteness of the resulting norms. It supplies the explicit label-derivative constant three and primitive constant two. Products may be any continuous bilinear map, with its operator norm included; the constants are independent of the fields, scales and time weight. The finite norms count every mixed multi-index once after division by $\gamma$. Periodicity of period one is needed for the phase operators, and zero phase average is additionally needed for the primitive. Those operations take values in a real Banach space. The derivative and product estimates need neither periodicity nor zero average. For phase-independent fields the Hölder product estimate uses the maximum of the supremum and seminorm. Replacing this by their sum alters only the order-dependent constant, leaving the paper's stated estimate intact.
